item.description:
• A new look. The window's backgrounds now match each other in light and dark mode, the MacBreeze name sits centred at the top, and one MacBreeze blue is used throughout. Warm and hot colours are easier to read in light mode.
  • The Overview shows CPU and GPU in cards of their own: the temperature, a word for how hot it is (Normal, Warm or Hot), and a graph of the last five minutes. Battery, Wi-Fi, power draw and battery drain sit in a row underneath.
  • Temperatures for each CPU core are now an option in Preferences, off by default. While it is off, MacBreeze doesn't read them at all.
  • The menu bar panel shows CPU and GPU first and larger, with the same words, and the speed of each fan.
  • Profiles and App Automations now say what each one sets, with a small picture of its fan curve. When two automated apps are open at once, you choose plainly which one wins: the app in front, or the one higher in the list.
  • The fan curve editor is cleaner: temperatures in even 10° steps, a dot showing where your fans are right now, and no legend to read.
  • If the fan helper stops responding, for example when macOS blocks it after a restart, MacBreeze now reinstalls it on its own, up to five times, instead of waiting for you to click Reinstall.

• Auto-Blast no longer goes off on a brief temperature spike. It now waits for 4 seconds of continuous heat before running the fans at full speed. If macOS itself reports a critical temperature, Auto-Blast still starts straight away.
  • When Auto-Blast ends, the fans now slow down step by step over a few seconds instead of dropping straight back to normal speed.
  • The battery's charge and drain time now appears within seconds of plugging in or unplugging. MacBreeze reads the same estimate macOS uses for its own battery icon, instead of waiting many minutes to work it out itself.
  • The menu bar item's text is now centered, and the Compact size is noticeably smaller.
  • Fixed: after you reinstalled the fan helper, the "not on the latest version" warning could stay on screen even though the helper was up to date.

• Fixed: battery temperature was missing on some Macs. MacBreeze was reading it from the wrong place in macOS and found nothing; it now reads it from where the battery actually reports it.
  • Fixed: after an update, the fan helper could keep running its older code until you restarted your Mac. MacBreeze now notices when the helper is behind and restarts it, so fixes to it take effect straight away.
  • The menu bar no longer shifts sideways while MacBreeze works out your battery's charge or drain rate. The long "Calculating…" is now a small hourglass that takes the same space as the reading, so the icons next to MacBreeze stay put.
  • Right after you plug in the charger, MacBreeze shows the hourglass instead of the plug. macOS can take half a minute or more to start charging, and the plug made it look as if the Mac wouldn't charge.
  • Fixed: the battery hourglass could stay up forever at ordinary drain rates and never settle on a reading.
